It allows teams to organize tasks, share files, set deadlines, and track time directly on tasks. It's designed to streamline the workflow of both small teams and large enterprises. ActiveCollab also includes invoicing and client management features, making it a versatile tool for managing all aspects of a project.

technologies.name: FreeRTOS
technologies.description: FreeRTOS is a real-time operating system kernel for embedded devices.
technologies.explanation: FreeRTOS is an open-source, miniaturized real-time operating system kernel designed for microcontrollers and small microprocessors. It provides a simple, lightweight, and scalable solution for managing hardware resources and allows developers to focus on building the actual application features.

technologies.name: TCP/IP
technologies.description: TCP/IP is the foundational protocol suite for the internet, enabling communication between diverse computer systems.
technologies.explanation: TCP/IP, or Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol, is a set of communication protocols used to interconnect network devices on the internet. TCP/IP specifies how data should be packetized, addressed, transmitted, routed, and received. This protocol suite has been standardized and is the basis for the global network of networks that is the internet.

technologies.name: Linux Drivers
technologies.description: Linux drivers are the software layers that allow hardware devices to communicate effectively with Linux-based operating systems.
technologies.explanation: Linux drivers are critical components that enable the Linux kernel to interface with various hardware devices, such as graphics cards, network adapters, and storage devices. They are developed by a combination of community contributors, hardware manufacturers, and organizations, ensuring broad hardware compatibility for Linux systems.

technologies.name: ASP.NET Core
technologies.description: ASP.NET Core is a free, open-source, high-performance web framework for building modern, cloud-based, Internet-connected applications.
technologies.explanation: ASP.NET Core is a cross-platform web framework developed by Microsoft. It allows developers to build dynamic web sites, applications, and services. It is the successor to the ASP.NET framework, redesigned to provide a modular, lean, and high-performance environment that can run on Windows, Linux, and macOS.

technologies.name: OpenEdge
technologies.description: OpenEdge is an integrated development environment for building dynamic multi-language applications.
technologies.explanation: OpenEdge, developed by Progress Software, is a platform for building high-performance business applications that can run on any platform and any database. It includes a development environment, application server, and database, all optimized for operational efficiency and scalability.

technologies.name: PhoneGap
technologies.description: PhoneGap is an open-source framework for building cross-platform mobile applications using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
technologies.explanation: PhoneGap allows developers to create applications for a variety of mobile platforms using a single codebase. It wraps web applications in a native container which can access device functions across various platforms. PhoneGap is powered by Apache Cordova and has been instrumental in the advancement of hybrid mobile app development.

technologies.name: DSP
technologies.description: DSP stands for Digital Signal Processing, a field of study and application of signal processing on digital signals.
technologies.explanation: Digital Signal Processing (DSP) involves the analysis, modification, and synthesis of signals such as sound, images, and biological measurements. DSP techniques are used to improve the accuracy and reliability of digital communications by manipulating digital data to achieve higher performance in various systems.

technologies.name: Google App Engine
technologies.description: Google App Engine is a fully managed, serverless platform for developing and hosting web applications at scale.
technologies.explanation: Google App Engine allows developers to build highly scalable applications on a fully managed serverless platform. It supports popular languages such as Java, Python, and Node.js, and eliminates the need to manage infrastructure, allowing developers to focus on code. With automatic scaling, load balancing, and robust security, App Engine enables developers to deploy applications quickly and with minimal operational overhead.

technologies.name: Alpine Linux
technologies.description: Alpine Linux is a security-oriented, lightweight Linux distribution based on musl libc and busybox.
technologies.explanation: Alpine Linux is designed for power users who appreciate security, simplicity, and resource efficiency. It uses its own package management system, apk-tools, and is commonly used in container environments due to its small size. Alpine Linux is often chosen for server installations and embedded systems due to its low overhead and high performance.

technologies.name: Mocha
technologies.description: Mocha is a feature-rich JavaScript test framework running on Node.js and in the browser.
technologies.explanation: Mocha is a flexible testing framework for JavaScript that provides a simple API for writing test cases. It supports asynchronous testing, test coverage reports, and use of any assertion library. Mocha is often used in combination with assertion libraries such as Chai, Sinon, and proxyquire to provide a robust testing suite.

technologies.name: Java Swing
technologies.description: Java Swing is a GUI widget toolkit for Java.
technologies.explanation: Java Swing is part of Oracle's Java Foundation Classes (JFC) – an API for providing a graphical user interface (GUI) for Java programs. It is a lightweight component framework that leverages the Java language's cross-platform capabilities.

technologies.name: SignalR
technologies.description: SignalR is a library for ASP.NET developers that simplifies the process of adding real-time web functionality to applications.
technologies.explanation: SignalR is an open-source library that enables real-time communication between server and client applications. It uses WebSockets when available and falls back to other compatible techniques for older browsers. SignalR allows bi-directional communication and can scale to handle high traffic.

technologies.name: XML
technologies.description: XML (eXtensible Markup Language) is a markup language that defines a set of rules for encoding documents in a format that is both human-readable and machine-readable.
technologies.explanation: XML is a flexible text format originally designed to meet the challenges of large-scale electronic publishing. XML is also used for representing arbitrary data structures, such as those used in web services. It allows designers to create their own custom tags, enabling the definition, transmission, validation, and interpretation of data between applications and between organizations.

technologies.name: iPadOS
technologies.description: iPadOS is the operating system designed specifically for the iPad by Apple.
technologies.explanation: iPadOS is a mobile operating system created and developed by Apple Inc. for its iPad line of tablet computers. It builds on the same foundation as iOS, but includes distinct features for the larger display of the iPad, such as improved multitasking and gesture navigation.

technologies.name: Retrofit
technologies.description: Retrofit is a type-safe HTTP client for Android and Java.
technologies.explanation: Retrofit turns your HTTP API into a Java interface. It makes it relatively easy to retrieve and upload JSON (or other structured data) via a REST based webservice. With annotations, you can easily serialize and deserialize API calls and responses.

technologies.name: Combine
technologies.description: A framework by Apple for handling asynchronous events by combining event-processing operators.
technologies.explanation: Combine is a declarative Swift API for processing values over time. It provides a functional reactive programming (FRP) approach, enabling developers to compose and transform sequences of values. Combine integrates with the Swift ecosystem, supporting Swift's features like type safety and error handling. It simplifies the creation of complex, asynchronous UIs and data streams, making code more readable and maintainable.

technologies.name: Realm
technologies.description: Realm is a mobile database that runs directly inside phones, tablets or wearables.
technologies.explanation: Realm is an open-source object database management system, initially designed for mobile operating systems such as iOS and Android. It aims to provide a more efficient alternative to SQLite and Core Data through its live objects and real-time data synchronization features. Realm databases are directly exposed to the end-devices, providing offline capabilities and reducing server-side dependencies.

technologies.name: Room
technologies.description: Room provides an abstraction layer over SQLite to allow for more robust database access while harnessing the full power of SQLite.
technologies.explanation: The Room persistence library provides an abstraction layer over SQLite to allow fluent database access while harnessing the full power of SQLite. The library helps with creating a cache of your app's data on a device that's running your app, which allows for direct queries and ensures that users can view consistent data while offline. Room also verifies SQL queries at compile time, which greatly adds to the security and robustness of your app by catching potential issues early in the development process.

technologies.name: Android NDK
technologies.description: The Android NDK is a toolset that allows developers to implement parts of their app using native-code languages such as C and C++.
technologies.explanation: Android NDK stands for Native Development Kit, and it's a set of tools that allows developers to use C and C++ code with Android. It bridges the gap between the performance of native applications and the convenience of Java-based Android development. The NDK is used to optimize performance-critical portions of apps.

technologies.name: Faust
technologies.description: Faust is a functional programming language specifically designed for real-time signal processing and synthesis.
technologies.explanation: Faust (Functional Audio Stream) is a programming language for sound synthesis and audio processing with a focus on the design of synthesizers, musical effects, or virtual instruments. It provides a high-level functional approach to signal processing with a strong mathematical foundation and efficient C++ code generation.

technologies.name: FastAPI
technologies.description: FastAPI is a modern, fast web framework for building APIs with Python based on standard Python type hints.
technologies.explanation: FastAPI is a high-performance web framework for building APIs with Python 3.7+ based on Pydantic and Starlette. It's designed to create APIs that are easy to code and highly type-safe while also enabling high performance. FastAPI facilitates the creation of RESTful APIs with automatic interactive API documentation using Swagger UI and ReDoc.

technologies.name: RDS
technologies.description: Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) makes it easy to set up, operate, and scale a relational database in the cloud.
technologies.explanation: Amazon RDS is a managed database service that provides you with six familiar database engines including Amazon Aurora, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle Database, and SQL Server. It handles routine database tasks such as provisioning, patching, backup, recovery, failure detection, and repair. Users can easily manage through the AWS Management Console or the AWS Command Line Interface.

technologies.name: AWS SQS
technologies.description: AWS SQS (Simple Queue Service) is a fully managed message queuing service.
technologies.explanation: Amazon SQS offers a secure, durable, and available hosted queue that lets you integrate and decouple distributed software systems and components. AWS SQS supports a range of message sizes and throughput, providing a scalable solution for messaging.

technologies.name: AWS Api Gateway
technologies.description: AWS API Gateway is a fully managed service that makes it easy for developers to create, publish, maintain, monitor, and secure APIs at any scale.
technologies.explanation: Amazon API Gateway handles all the tasks involved in accepting and processing up to hundreds of thousands of concurrent API calls, including traffic management, authorization and access control, monitoring, and API version management. It provides developers with high-availability, low-latency access to backend services, and integrates seamlessly with other AWS services.

technologies.name: Cisco
technologies.description: Cisco is a global leader in networking and cybersecurity solutions.
technologies.explanation: Cisco Systems, Inc. is an American multinational technology conglomerate headquartered in San Jose, California, in the center of Silicon Valley. Cisco develops, manufactures, and sells networking hardware, software, telecommunications equipment, and other high-technology services and products.

technologies.name: Microsoft Hyper-V
technologies.description: Microsoft Hyper-V is a virtualization platform that enables running multiple operating systems on a single physical server.
technologies.explanation: Microsoft Hyper-V is a hypervisor-based technology that provides enterprise-level virtualization for x86-64 systems. It allows IT administrators to create and manage a virtualized computing environment, improving server utilization and reducing costs. Hyper-V supports creating virtual machines, each running its own operating system independently. It integrates with Windows Server but also offers versions that work with Windows 10 and 11 for development and testing purposes. Its features include live migrations, extensible virtual switch, and shielded VMs for enhanced security.

technologies.name: AWS Developer Tools
technologies.description: AWS Developer Tools is a set of services designed to enable developers to build, test, and deploy applications on AWS.
technologies.explanation: AWS Developer Tools is a collection of services that facilitate software development and continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) on the AWS platform. These tools integrate with AWS services and third-party tools, offering a scalable and flexible solution for managing complex application development workflows.

technologies.name: Azure DevOps Pipelines
technologies.description: Azure DevOps Pipelines is a cloud service that automates the build, testing, and deployment of applications.
technologies.explanation: Azure DevOps Pipelines provides a rich set of features that support continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) for developing and deploying applications. It integrates with various version control systems and provides a robust mechanism for automating and managing the application lifecycle.

technologies.name: AWS CloudWatch
technologies.description: AWS CloudWatch is a monitoring and observability service designed for DevOps engineers, developers, site reliability engineers (SREs), and IT managers.
technologies.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch provides data and actionable insights to monitor applications, understand and respond to system-wide performance changes, optimize resource utilization, and get a unified view of operational health. CloudWatch collects monitoring and operational data in the form of logs, metrics, and events, providing you with a complete overview of your AWS resources, applications, and services that run on AWS and on-premises servers.

technologies.name: Dart
technologies.description: Dart is an open-source, scalable programming language, with robust libraries and runtimes, for building web, server, and mobile apps.
technologies.explanation: Dart is a client-optimized language for fast apps on any platform. It is developed by Google and is used to build mobile, desktop, backend, and web applications. Dart is particularly known for being the language behind Flutter, Google's UI toolkit for building natively compiled applications for mobile, web, and desktop from a single codebase.

technologies.name: Kubeflow
technologies.description: Kubeflow is an open-source machine learning platform designed to deploy, monitor, and manage ML workflows on Kubernetes.
technologies.explanation: Kubeflow is a Kubernetes-native platform for developing, orchestrating, deploying, and running scalable and portable machine learning workloads. It provides a set of tools to support the entire machine learning lifecycle, including experimentation, training, tuning, and serving. It is designed to be flexible and to integrate with other tools easily.

technologies.name: CircleCI
technologies.description: CircleCI is a continuous integration and delivery platform that automates the software development process.
technologies.explanation: CircleCI enables developers to rapidly build, test, and deploy their code in a consistent and reliable manner. It integrates seamlessly with GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, and Bitbucket. CircleCI supports dockerized environments along with macOS and Linux virtual machines. The platform offers a configuration-as-code approach, making it highly customizable to fit various development workflows.

technologies.name: AWS CDK
technologies.description: AWS CDK is an open-source software development framework to define cloud infrastructure in code and provision it through AWS CloudFormation.
technologies.explanation: The AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK) is a software development framework for defining cloud infrastructure in code and provisioning it through AWS CloudFormation. It provides high-level components that preconfigure cloud resources with proven defaults, so you can build cloud applications without needing to be an expert in AWS services.

technologies.name: Red Hat Quay
technologies.description: Red Hat Quay is a private container registry that stores, builds, and deploys container images.
technologies.explanation: Red Hat Quay is a secure, scalable, and reliable container image registry developed by Red Hat. It supports Docker and Kubernetes formats and provides features like image scanning, geographic replication, and automated builds. It's designed for enterprise-grade deployments with support for high availability configurations.

technologies.name: tvOS
technologies.description: tvOS is the operating system for Apple TV, providing a home for Apple TV apps and games.
technologies.explanation: tvOS is an operating system developed by Apple Inc. specifically for its Apple TV hardware platform. It enables users to stream multimedia content, download and use apps, play games, and more. The platform is designed to integrate seamlessly with other Apple services and devices, offering a unified ecosystem. tvOS supports Siri voice commands and the Apple TV app, which centralizes content from various streaming services.

technologies.name: Android TV
